_comment: Copy to ~/.config/capocantiere/workers.json and keep only what you change: missing keys use the built-in defaults. Keys starting with _ are comments. Environment variables CAPOCANTIERE_<WORKER>_<SETTING> (e.g. CAPOCANTIERE_VIBE_MAX_PRICE=1) override this file.
_order: Preference order when no worker is requested (the session default from /capocantiere:use goes first).
_fallback: On a quota/rate-limit error or an exhausted budget, move the job to the next worker.
_max_parallel: Jobs running at once across all workers (each worker also has its own max_parallel).
_isolation: How worker processes are isolated: none, auto (the backend of this system), bwrap (Linux), seatbelt (macOS, EXPERIMENTAL). A worker whose isolation cannot work is skipped, never run unisolated. Each worker can override it. Check what is missing with /capocantiere:doctor.
_keyring_dbus_names: Linux, "host" credentials: the only session D-Bus services an isolated worker can reach (through xdg-dbus-proxy), i.e. the system keyring.
_selection: How a worker is chosen when none is requested (and no session default): "scores" ranks every worker:model by its trust score with Thompson sampling (the order only breaks ties while there is no history), "order" always follows the preference order. See /capocantiere:scores.
_half_life_days: Trust score events lose half their weight every N days (models and CLIs change).

copilot._comment: GitHub Copilot CLI. Logs in with `copilot login`. daily_budget counts runs (each run costs AI credits / premium requests). deny_tools are always denied while auto-approving in the job's worktree.
copilot._credentials: "host": the login of the CLI itself (copilot login, in the system keyring). "token": a fine-grained personal access token with only the "Copilot Requests" permission, read from ~/.local/state/capocantiere/credentials/copilot (chmod 600) or CAPOCANTIERE_COPILOT_TOKEN and given to this worker only, as COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN. Same for vibe (MISTRAL_API_KEY) and agy (GEMINI_API_KEY).
copilot._isolation: Empty = the global setting. isolation_rw / isolation_ro: extra paths the isolated worker may write / read; isolation_env: extra environment variables it keeps (names, or prefixes ending in "_").
copilot._tiers: Models per capability tier, e.g. {"fast": "<model>", "standard": "<model>", "strong": ["<model>", "<model>"]}: delegate/analyze pick one with tier. Each model is a separate arm for the trust scores. Empty = this worker serves every tier with its model setting. For agy, without tiers a tier is the model group of the same name.

vibe._comment: Mistral Vibe CLI. Signs in with your Mistral account (run `vibe` once; the Free plan works) or MISTRAL_API_KEY. max_price is a USD cap per run computed from vibe's configured prices: an extra guard only. Set outside_workdir = "deny" in ~/.vibe/config.toml.

codex._comment: OpenAI Codex CLI, with your own `codex login` (any ChatGPT plan, Free included, or an API key). Put cli_auth_credentials_store = "file" in ~/.codex/config.toml: the login is then auth.json and an isolated run needs no D-Bus. max_parallel 1 is a precaution (runs share the login's token refreshes).
codex._sandbox: Codex's own sandbox: read-only for analyses, workspace-write for jobs. It nests inside the server's isolation. false = danger-full-access, allowed only with isolation on.
codex._network_access: Network for the commands Codex runs in a job (its workspace-write sandbox).
codex._credentials: "host": your ~/.codex login (mounted read-write when isolated, Codex refreshes its token there). "token": an OpenAI API key as CODEX_API_KEY. "private-home": a separate CODEX_HOME for capocantiere only (~/.local/state/capocantiere/homes/codex), with its own file-based login.

agy._comment: Antigravity CLI. DISABLED by default: running `agy -p` inside third-party agents is not supported on consumer plans and can get the account suspended. Enable it only with an API key, never with the subscription login.
agy._auth: api_key: Gemini API key from AI Studio in GEMINI_API_KEY (export it, or set it under env); adc: Google Cloud Application Default Credentials; login: the signed-in Google account (NOT recommended, see above).
